verses.1: Woe to those who plot iniquity and work evil on their beds while the morning light still shines, for they have strength in their hands.
verses.2: They covet fields and seize them, steal houses and take them. They oppress men and their homes, men and their inheritances.
verses.3: Therefore, the Lord says: I will plan evil against this family, and you will not escape punishment. Your throats will remain stiff, and you will not walk proudly, for it is an evil time.
verses.4: On that day a parable will be taken up against you, and a lament will be sung, saying: "We have been plundered, we have been ruined. Our portion was measured with a rope, but no one stopped us from turning back. Our fields have been divided."
verses.5: Therefore, you will not cast a line in your inheritance within the assembly of the Lord.
verses.6: Do not weep for them, do not weep for them, for they will not accept your comfort. For they have drawn their lot, and they will not be spared.
verses.7: Is it said in the house of Jacob: "Is the anger of the Lord short?" Or, "Are these his deeds?" No, his words are upright, and his path is straight.
verses.8: My people will be taken up by an enemy. With a false peace they will be led away, like captives taken by those who do not fight.
verses.9: The leaders of my people will be driven from their houses of luxury. Because of their wicked schemes, they will be cast out. They have drawn near to the mountains for eternity.
verses.10: Arise and go, for this is not your resting place, because of the defilement that brought you to ruin. You are broken beyond repair.
verses.11: If a man walks in deceit and falsehood, and lies to you with wine and drink, then this people will be doomed by their own lying.
verses.12: I will gather all Jacob and collect the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the middle of their resting place. They will be safe from human harm.
verses.13: The one who breaks through goes ahead of them, breaking through and passing through the gate, and their king passes ahead of them. The Lord is at their head.

notes:
Notes  
- v. 1: The translation of *cheshbon* (חֶשְׁב֖וֹן) is "plot" or "reckon," and fits the context of scheming iniquity.  
- v. 5: "You will not cast a line in your inheritance" is a poetic rendering of the Hebrew, which speaks of not being able to cast a rope to claim a portion, symbolizing loss of property.  
- v. 13: The phrase is metaphorical, using the imagery of a shepherd guiding his flock, with the king and the Lord leading the people forward.
